How do you feel about open relationships? Open marriages etc..?
I think that they require a great deal of communication and honesty about feelings. I have friends that have open marriages. Done well, it's great. Done poorly, it's a festering ground of resentment.

I'm all for them. Humans are only animals, this stuff about morality and the sanctity of marriage is bullshit. Marriage (both polygamous and monogamous) are only good for raising children, and even then you don't need a fucking piece of paper or a metal band to properly raise a child.
I'm for it if my partner is for it, with exceptions. I think it should be discussed, even if it's to rule it out.

i have one friend who is in a few open relationships. It seems to be a very close knit group that has rules about kids, and they get along well. I even think it should be legalized.

Personally though, I feel like I would rather spend all time with one person, than chase after adventures with others. Sure, more and creative sex would be great, having that romance phase with someone new is tempting, and seriously, you will have crushes on other people. But I only have so many years on earth, and I found a great partner, I would rather focus my time on her and my children.

I worked with someone who was in an open marriage and would openly parade around with his wife and girlfriend. It's weird. People talked behind his back. Mostly made fun of him. Personally, I didn't care and didn't judge them. Good for him, I guess.

Why label it? Why place limits on something that you're trying to leave open? Identifying it seems illogical. I can understand in theory why this works for some, but I wouldn't want it. I like having my best friend and significant other who is not legally bound to me or required to be with me, but we add to one another's lives. We made individual choices to pursue our dreams and passions alone, and on the way found one another. I feel more free than I ever have before and I feel a relationship title has nothing to do with it. I found my best friend in him, my inspiration. So open relationships to me, need not be explained or defined. It just is. I'm all for those who know that is what they desire. Then they know themselves pretty damn well. So kudos to that. I appreciate anyone who knows what they want and refuse to settle on less.
Indifferent. It's not for me, no kind of marriage is.

In order for it to work, the people involved need to have a solid relationship, excellent communication, and good self-esteem. If any of those is lacking, it is almost certainly doomed. Ground rules need to be made clear and adjusted as needed.
They don't work, exclusively. Anyone who claims they do haven't given it enough time.

For all of you interested in swinging and non-monogamous relationships come on over to v/swingers. We are still growing but we are there to answer questions you might have and might be able to walk you through important parts of swinging.

I think that if it makes those people happy, then they should be free to do it. Same goes for polygamy, as long as no one is coerced into it, I have no problem with it. It's not my thing, but different strokes for different folks. None of it should be illegal.

Agreed. It seems potentially tricky, but I have don't doubt that many people are better-wired for it. It seems like an ungodly amount of work to me; I barely have time to have one relationship and still have enough time to myself to pursue my own career, hobbies, and interests, so I couldn't imagine trying to float multiple relationships at the same time.
Someone is unhappy, while the other person is really happy, thats what i think about open marriage.
I'm a selfish person, so I don't think it would work for me. But I believe that there are some people for who it's ok, so I'm happy for them.
Being in a relationship and still having to chase strange seems like the worst of both worlds. It's like buying a private jet, but still flying commercial.
I personally couldn't handle it. I correlate sex and physical intimacy with emotional intimacy with people I care about. If it's just a fwb, it could be different.

Allow anyone who wishes to to abstain from donating to the fund and sure. Once you start forcing people to contribute to causes that you agree with and they don't then you are no longer advocating for libertarianism. That is one of my favorite parts of libertarianism. We don't want to force anyone else to be libertarian while democrats and republicans both want to force their own values on people.

I do not believe it is possible to achieve purely voluntary contribution. Limited government complexity is more important to me than limited government economic influence. I'm more worried about corruption and waste than economic redistribution. The economy is a game and the government is the referee. It's best if the game is simple enough that the players can understand it. Overly limiting the tools the referees have to dissuade cheating seems like an invitation for disorder.

A pure libertarian would believe that the increase in happiness would never be worth the decrease in liberty caused by forcing Warren Buffett to give a waitress $50, or would actually deny the truth that it increases happiness. I believe the rules of the economic game should be designed to give advantages to the people who are losing.

Firstly, a mon is a symbol on kimono signifying the wearer's okiya, a way for the okiya to mark its kimono to show it owns it. Kuromontsuki (formal kimono) are crested with 5 mon, but there are crested non-black kimono also.

I encourage you to click through the links to see the scans of vintage books, and read the information.

Yield For Kimono posted a series on an obi she bought online which had a mon on it which didn't correspond with an okiya. It's a swirly kiku symbol.

Part 1: Dude, it's a darari!

She had been looking through vintage photos for this mon, finding it in a photo from 1974. Then, she spotted it on youtube:

Part 2: Mystery mon, kind of solved?

An obi worn by Mameharu has the same mon, and is very similar to the obi above.

There is another known instance in which Tama has had their girls wearing another crest. IG member Golden_Phoenix has one of several hikizuri which different Tama geiko have worn for Hassaku the past several years, which features a closed-fan mon. You can read about her experience here. Recently, a photo has been discovered of one of the hiki that points to it being worn around 1960. The book which has the photo of my mon is from 1974. The Tama okiya wasn’t founded until the 1980s, so she believes it likely that Tama absorbed one (or more, as the mon seem to indicate) okiya which had shut down and used their hikizuri and obi.

Part 3: Darari mystery mon

With help from IG users, YFK is able to piece together bits of the story. She is sent a photo of Manaha (Tama) wearing a hikizuri which was worn in a book in 1975, with an obi bearing the kikyo mon.

Ryuu-mori-Danna believes that the okiya which origally owned this mon was maybe the sponsoring okiya of Tama, or perhaps Tama used this mon until it could order obi with it’s own mon. He thinks it might also possibly be the okiya mon of Takeha, who is the older sister of all the “Tama” girls. (By the way, Tamakazu founded the Tama ochaya in 1972, and the okiya in 1987 according to his timeline on this photo).

More on Tamakazu later. So, Tama okiya, the mystery mon and the mystery mon's original okiya are linked somehow.

Part 4: Kikyo knot mon

YFK has been sent many more photos, and from them is able to discern the name of a senior maiko who was in the okiya.

Then, most excitingly, this next photo provides the first confirmed name of a maiko from this okiya….Mamekazu! (豆賀寿)

The next part is following Mamekazu's career:

According to the programs and other photos, Mamekazu became a maiko sometime between 1982-1983, turned geiko between 1987-1990, and retired between the 1993 and 1994 odori. This means that she was still working after her okiya closed, and Tama okiya took over the mon. Tamakazu, the founder of Tama okiya, opened her yakata in 1987, only two years after this book was published. In fact, there is a photo below of Mamekazu as a senior maiko in 1987, so one wonders how the fact that her okiya closed that year affected her career.

She also notes that Tama and the mystery okiya (synonym "yakata") share a naming convention which is still in use today, "Mame-". But, we know the okiya Tamakazu was from prior to splitting off and starting Tama okiya, and her mon looked nothing like it. If Mamekazu was still active until 1993/4. was she part of another okiya or was she jimae?

Part 5: Kikyo knot mon

It is the crest of an okiya which apparently closed sometime during the 1980s, and items with this mon have been occasionally used by the Tama okiya for their maiko.

Until Nishimura maiko started wearing it, that is. Back in 2011 there was a maiko called Keiko, who unfortunately "ran away" (an unusual choice of words, as maiko these days choose to work here, and can leave when they want). She wore a ro hikizuri featuring the kikyo mon to Hassaku that year.

<Until now, Tama was the only okiya which was documented to have their girls wear alternate crests on Hassaku, as well as being the only okiya which used the kikyou knot mon. Now, it seems that not only does Nishimura do it, but that they use the same mon that Tama sometimes does! As far as I know, there is no connection between Tama and Nishimura. The only explanation that I can think of is that there is a shortage of ro kuromontsuki kimono (which are only worn once a year on August 1st, and therefore one of the rarest kinds of kimono), and since Nishimura had three maiko in 2010, they might not have had enough for all of their girls to wear, and they had to borrow a kimono from Tama? Perhaps there is an exchange system between okiya which allows them to borrow from each other if they run out of an item?

Oh, I hope she is able to find out more about this mystery mon and okiya. Fingers crossed!
